title: observability-token-kv-alert-tuning-enhancements
author: Nadia Patel
description: Summary: Add token-level KV-cache metrics, improve logging for cache misses/hits, add new Grafana dashboards and curated alert tuning for token-level cost and latency spikes. Motivation: Recent incidents showed noisy token-level cost spikes and under-instrumented KV cache behavior leading to missed autoscaling and poor cost attribution. This change provides higher-fidelity visibility and safer alert defaults so on-call can triage regressions without false positives. What changed: 1) Metrics: add obs.redwood.kv.token_hits_total, obs.redwood.kv.token_misses_total, obs.redwood.kv.cache_evictions_total, obs.redwood.kv.token_latency_seconds histogram with labels model, pool, tenant, route; 2) Tracing: attach kv_cache.{hit|miss} attributes to existing inference spans and add a kv_cache eviction span for long-running compactions; 3) Logging: structured debug logs for rare miss-threshold events (rate-limited by default); 4) Dashboards: new Grafana dashboard panels for token-level cost/latency breakdowns, KV hit-rate heatmaps, eviction timelines, and tenant-level cost attribution; 5) Alerts: introduce tuned alerts to surface sustained token-latency regressions and cost-per-token anomalies with adaptive thresholds and 15m confirmation windows. Rollout: metrics and tracing are backwards-compatible; dashboards are added to observability config and will be introduced to prod via a staged rollout (canary -> 50% -> 100%). Migration notes: older dashboards will remain until teams switch over; alert configs include a safe default that will not fire for existing baselines. Tests: unit tests for metric registration, integration tests validating histogram buckets and tracing attachment, and dashboard smoke tests included. Checklist: - [x] Metric names and labels reviewed - [x] Tracing spans and attributes reviewed - [x] Dashboard UX reviewed with SRE - [x] Alert thresholds validated against 30d baseline - [x] Canary rollout plan documented in Linear (ENG-1428) Backwards compatibility: no breaking API changes. See linked Linear tickets for rollout schedule.
